newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate approves general telecom law.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate approves general telecom law.

text.p: The Brazilian Senate approved Thursday a bill authorizing the privatization of federally owned telecommunications firm Telebras and its subsidiaries, a Senate official said.
The General Telecommunications Law, which was approved by a vote of 58-13, will also create a new regulator to oversee the sector and set down rules for privately-owned operators.
The Senate was due to continue voting on several amendments proposed by senators opposed to the bill.
The text of the bill was unchanged from a version approved in June this year in the Chamber of Deputies.

The bill does not limit foreign capital in the telecommunications sector but gives the Brazilian president powers to restrict non-Brazilian ownership of telecommunications operators on a case-by-case basis.
The bill creates a National Telecommunications Agency (ANTEL), a new regluator which will oversee the allocation of concessions for telecommunications operators.
ANTEL will also seek to ensure free competition in the sector and will regulate radio and television concessions and satellite services.
ANTEL, which is due to be set up within 90 days as a semi-independent body, will control tariffs offered by private operators for an initial three-year period, after which it may free up rates.
The bill must now be signed into law by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Next week the Senate is due to vote on a bill which would regulate the opening up of Brazil's oil and gas sector.
